stem: A debenture yields a nominal return of 12% per annum. An investor needs a real return of at least 7% per annum. What is the maximum inflation rate (to the nearest 0.01%) the investor can tolerate before the real return falls below 7%?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Simple subtraction: 12% - 7% = 5%, ignoring the Fisher multiplicative correction that reduces the tolerance slightly.
Reported the required real return (7%) as the maximum inflation the investor can tolerate.
Added nominal and real: 12% + 7% = 19%, misapplying the Fisher equation by adding rates instead of rearranging the multiplicative form.

explanation: Rearranging the Fisher equation: (1 + r_nom) = (1 + r_real)(1 + r_inf). So (1 + r_inf) = (1 + r_nom)/(1 + r_real) = 1.12/1.07 = 1.04673. Maximum tolerable inflation = 4.67%.

explanation_sections.punchline: Rearranging the Fisher equation back-solves for inflation given nominal and real.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: r_inf = (1 + r_nom)/(1 + r_real) - 1. Map: r_nom = 0.12, r_real = 0.07. Compute 1.12/1.07 = 1.04673. Max inflation = 4.67%. The setup decision is identifying this as a Fisher back-solve.
explanation_sections.lesson: To find the break-even inflation, rearrange the Fisher formula; never use simple subtraction.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 seconds. Compute 1.12/1.07 = 1.0467. Eliminate option 2 (simple subtraction) as the common trap.
